findings.title: »Project Granite« SAP wird Opfer von Hackerangriff
findings.summary_md: Der Spiegel broke the story on 26 November 2026 at 20:14 CET under the internal codename Project Granite, reporting that SAP was dealing with a hacking incident the company had acknowledged internally. The article, by Marcel Rosenbach, states that per company-internal sources the attackers targeted SAP's presence on GitHub and may have used agentic AI systems to help. A teaser segment behind the paywall adds that employee authentication tokens were stolen and used to copy and alter SAP source code.

findings.title: SAP von IT-Sicherheitsvorfall betroffen
findings.summary_md: IT-Journal reported on 26 November 2026 that an internal notice to SAP staff described an active IT security incident handled under the codename Project Granite, which had caused significant internal alarm over the preceding days. The notice quoted in the report says SAP had detected suspicious activity. The piece repeats Der Spiegel's account that attackers targeted SAP repositories on GitHub and, according to an insider, stole employee authentication tokens to manipulate and copy SAP source code, while noting SAP publishes public source code for numerous products and open source projects there.

findings.title: SAP: IT-Sicherheitsvorfall, haben verdächtige Aktivitäten identifiziert
findings.summary_md: Handelsblatt reported SAP's own confirmation on the evening of 26 November 2026, with the company stating it had identified suspicious activity and taken the necessary measures to protect customers and secure services. Per Handelsblatt information, SAP restricted access to GitHub, halted automated workflows in software development and replaced signing keys. The article documents that the incident was aimed at software development, following Der Spiegel's earlier report of a hacking attack, and that SAP said its investigation had so far found no evidence of unauthorised access to customer business data.
